thread:
alex_support: Heads-up — ACME SOC reports ~8k audit events missing from their SIEM for tenant acme-prod between 2026-03-10T10:00:00Z and 10:30:00Z. They say gap appeared right after our KMS rotation window at ~10:05. Ticket #12345. Anyone oncall?

maria_sre: :eyes: I'm oncall. Can you paste the manifest/sample object list and any forwarder logs you have? Any zero-byte shards or 403s?

alex_support: Pasting a small extract of the manifest we received from ACME (s3 listing):
```
s3://redwood-exports/acme-prod/2026/03/10/10/part-0001.gz 125MB
s3://redwood-exports/acme-prod/2026/03/10/10/part-0002.gz 130MB
s3://redwood-exports/acme-prod/2026/03/10/10/part-0003.gz 128MB
s3://redwood-exports/acme-prod/2026/03/10/10/part-0004.gz 121MB
s3://redwood-exports/acme-prod/2026/03/10/10/part-0005.gz 0B
s3://redwood-exports/acme-prod/2026/03/10/10/part-0006.gz 34MB
manifest.json -> 6 shards
```
They say SIEM drops the whole hour window while ingesting, counts off by ~8k events compared to audit DB.

kai_eng: I'm pulling forwarder logs for prod-exports. Quick find shows at 2026-03-10T10:06:12Z we rotated alias -> new CMK. Forwarder log snippet from worker export-3: 
```
2026-03-10T10:06:11Z INFO rewrap start old_kms=arn:aws:kms:...:key/old-kid
2026-03-10T10:06:12Z ERROR hsm_connector.go:142 auth fail: nonce mismatch (transient)
2026-03-10T10:06:12Z WARN write failed for shard part-0005, retry 1
2026-03-10T10:06:15Z INFO retry succeeded but atomic_upload=false, uploaded object size=0 for part-0005.gz
```
Looks like one worker hit an HSM auth error and then uploaded a zero-byte object during retry.

maria_sre: That matches ACME manifest (part-0005.gz 0B). SIEM parsers frequently drop truncated/zero-byte gz files. We should check gzip header integrity for neighboring parts, and verify whether the worker created a zero-byte placeholder. Can you dump the worker's local temp file?

jen_infra: I listed the S3 prefix; confirm: part-0005.gz = 0 bytes, part-0004.gz and part-0006.gz valid. I can try to reconstruct part-0005 from worker backups (we keep ephemeral backups for 24h). Recommend we do a controlled replay for 10:00-10:10 window.

alex_support: I informed ACME and asked them to pause their SIEM pipeline for that window until we finish replay. They asked for an ETA and exact replay steps to re-ingest.

kai_eng: Quick audit DB check: events for seq 1,234,500 - 1,243,999 map to that time chunk and are present in our DB. So data wasn't lost on producer side — this is export/packaging failure. Backfill plan: rewrap encrypted payloads with new CMK and reupload. Steps: 
```bash
# on infra worker with access to backups
export OLD_KEY=arn:aws:kms:us-east-1:123456:key/old-kid
export NEW_KEY=arn:aws:kms:us-east-1:123456:key/new-kid
./encryption-agent rewrap --input /backups/acme/2026-03-10/10 --old-key $OLD_KEY --new-key $NEW_KEY --atomic-upload --prefix replay/acme-prod/2026/03/10/10
```
Verify checksums after upload.

maria_sre: Important note: encryption-agent v2.1.0 has a known issue where interrupted rewrap can produce truncated gzip objects if --atomic-upload isn't used. Ops should ensure agent >=2.1.1 or use the flag. Also we need HSM connector retries hardened — transient nonce failures should backoff and not create zero-byte placeholders.

kms_hsm_bot: KMS rotation rot-20260310-7 completed at 2026-03-10T10:06:15Z. HSM console shows one transient AUTH_FAIL on connector-3 at 10:06:12Z; key material was successfully imported and rotation finalized. No further errors on subsequent connectors.

jen_infra: Running checksums now and reconstructing part-0005 from worker backup. Starting replay job in dry-run to validate SIEM parser accepts the reuploaded gz. Will not flip ACLs live until dry-run passes.

alex_support: I sent ACME a short note with our plan and the commands they'll see in ticket. They're ok with a short pause; they asked for postmortem and ETA. ETA for dry-run + replay?

kai_eng: Dry-run expected in ~45m, full replay within 2h assuming reconstruction succeeds. If reconstruction fails, we'll generate a synthesized shard from DB events and re-encode — that adds ~3h.

maria_sre: I'll own the postmortem. Root cause draft: (1) HSM transient auth failure during KMS rotation → worker retry path created zero-byte object; (2) encryption-agent v2.1.0 lacked atomic-upload guard causing truncated/empty shard; (3) SIEM parser drops invalid gz resulting in missing events. Action items: harden HSM connector retries, force encryption-agent bump to 2.1.1, add a validation step in forwarder to check gzip headers before upload, and add an alert for 0-byte shard uploads.

jen_infra: Update: reconstructed part-0005 from backup and re-encrypted/reuploaded to replay/acme-prod/2026/03/10/10/part-0005.gz (checksum matches). Started dry-run against SIEM endpoint — parser accepted gz and counted ~8,021 events.

alex_support: ACME confirms SIEM ingested backfill and counts match audit DB now. They're asking for final confirmation and the postmortem.

kai_eng: Closing loop: pushed hotfix to encryption-agent (2.1.1) with --atomic-upload enforced by default; patched forwarder retry to avoid creating placeholder zero-byte objects on transient HSM errors. Starting a scheduled job to revalidate past 24h exports for zero-byte anomalies.

maria_sre: :thumbsup: I'll attach the RCA to ticket #12345 and schedule an ops review for HSM connector SLAs. Thanks everyone.
